story: In the constellation Cygnus, 8,000 light-years away, a cosmic monster named V404 Cygni wakes up every few decades to feast. This system contains a black hole roughly ten times the mass of our Sun, locked in a tight orbit with a companion star. As the black hole strips gas from its partner, material piles up in a massive disk until it reaches a violent tipping point. During its 2015 outburst, it became the brightest object in the X-ray sky, outshining the Crab Nebula by 50 times. Most terrifyingly, the black hole doesn't just swallow matter—it spits. It fires high-speed plasma jets that wobble and change direction every few minutes. This cosmic 'jitter' is caused by the Lense-Thirring effect, where the black hole's immense gravity actually warps and drags the fabric of space-time as it spins. Even when 'sleeping,' this predator remains active, with recent telescope data showing its jets never truly turn off.
angle: The black hole's plasma jets wobble rapidly every few minutes because its spin is literally warping and dragging the fabric of space-time.
